transcription.testTitle: Common adjectives 1: Good and bad things

exercises.instruction: Put these adjectives into the correct columns.
Circle the correct underlined adjective in these sentences.
items: Example: Harry is a nice/dreadful man – nobody likes him.
1 I love Kay's new car – it's great/awful.
2 I don't like my boss – he's wonderful/horrible.
3 Let's go to Max's Restaurant tonight – the food there is nasty/excellent.
4 Pete didn't enjoy the film – he said it was awful/brilliant.
5 Sue did very well in her test – the teacher said she wrote a terrible/brilliant essay.
6 The party was terrible/lovely – everyone had a good time.
7 Thank you so much – I had a perfect/horrible day.
8 Jo does very well at school – she usually gets good/bad marks in her class.
9 We're planning to have a picnic tomorrow – I hope the weather is fine/terrible.
10 The hotel was awful/marvellous – we'll never go there again.

exercises.instruction: Fill the gaps in these dialogues. We give you the first letter each time.
items: Example: A: I had a great time at the party last night.
1 A: Let's meet at 7 – OK?
2 A: What dreadful weather!
3 A: I'll send you a postcard from our holiday.
4 A: The film was terrible, wasn't it!
5 A: The food is good here, isn't it?
6 A: I'll show you the town tomorrow.
7 A: I don't like her very much, do you?
8 A: I'll help you paint your room if you like.
9 A: It's a beautiful view, isn't it?
10 A: Did you enjoy the party?
